title: Shadow reservoir prefill and kernel-hint protocol for fragment deflation
creator: Anya Patel
body:
Problem: We observe repeated small, short-lived KV fragments that are repeatedly evicted and reloaded during bursty conversational workloads. This churn increases decode latency tail and increases wasted GPU memory traffic.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight "shadow reservoir" layer that temporarily holds a compact fingerprint+metadata for recently-evicted fragments and leverages probabilistic re-admission (sampling) to avoid thrash. In parallel, introduce a compact per-fragment "kernel signature" that encodes the preferred kernel candidate set (FP16/INT8, fused attention variant, sparse-aware path) derived from model-profile telemetry. On prefill, the scheduler consults the shadow reservoir and kernel signature to: 1) decide fast rehydrate vs cold fetch, 2) select a warm kernel bin to reduce JIT/warmstart penalties, and 3) apply a short anti-starvation decode holdback for fragments with high re-admission probability to avoid head-of-line eviction storms.

Design notes: Shadow reservoir is not a full KV store: it keeps 64B fingerprint (Bloom-friendly), a 16-bit touch counter decay, and a 16-bit admission score. Reservoir entries are kept in a per-shard compact ring with configurable TTL and adaptive sampling rate based on eviction rate. Kernel signature is a 3-bit compact enum plus a 1-byte confidence score; it is produced at model onboarding and refined online by lightweight telemetry (10K recent calls sampling).

Trade-offs considered:
- Full persistent LRU per-tenant would reduce misses but increases memory and GC complexity; shadow reservoir trades perfect recall for minimal memory.
- Adding kernel signatures increases metadata writes on slot allocation; we batch writes into allocation epochs to reduce write amplification.
- Anti-starvation holdback can slightly increase median latency for a small fraction of requests; we gate it behind SLO-aware policies and a max hold window.

Success metrics (target):
- Reduce repeated fragment rehydrate rate by >= 35% on conversational traces.
- Reduce 99th percentile decode latency by >= 12% for medium-length (512 token) sequences in tenant-heavy experiments.
- Additional metadata memory overhead < 1.5% of total KV footprint.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow reservoir deployed behind a feature flag in a single runtime pool
Bench harness shows >=35% reduction in repeated rehydrates on 5 representative tenant traces
P99 decode latency regression <= 5% for stable workloads when feature flag enabled
End-to-end e2e test coverage for reservoir TTL, admission sampling, and kernel-signature fallback
steps: Implement compact reservoir slot format and per-shard ring in runtime-storage module
Add kernel-signature field to model-profile pipeline and runtime metadata APIs
Implement prefill scheduler consult: reservoir check -> admission sampling -> kernel hint lookup
Create microbench harness with recorded tenant traces (3 medium, 2 heavy) and run A/B experiments
Roll out behind feature flag to canary pool (10% of production traffic) and monitor eviction/reload metrics
Iterate on sampling thresholds and TTLs based on canary telemetry, then scale rollout
comments: 2026-02-26 - Anya Patel: Filed a quick spec draft and sketched the reservoir proto layout. Linking the Confluence doc above.

2026-03-02 - Diego Morales: Prototype implemented in runtime-storage branch 'shadow-reservoir/proto'. Basic in-memory ring validated with unit tests. Observed ~28% reduction in rehydrates on synthetic burst trace A.
2026-03-05 - Priya Nair (Product): Confirmed customer cases (chatbot customers) where cross-tenant bursts cause repeated eviction. Prioritize for runtime-1.24 if experiments hold.
2026-03-08 - Elena (SRE): Canary infra prepared; added exporter metrics: reservoir_hits, reservoir_admits, kernel_signature_lookups, admission_holdbacks. Scheduled canary run.

2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Canary run started at 03/12:10:00 UTC on pool 'canary-03' (10% traffic). Early telemetry shows reservoir_admits=14.2% and repeated rehydrate delta ~34% after 6 hours. No SLO alerts.
2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Next: tune sampling floor and add safety cap to admission score to prevent long-lived ghost entries. Will open PR for canary tuning.
2026-03-12 - Security (note): Reviewed metadata footprint and found no new PII vectors; security_review_required set to false.
notes: Prototype uses MurmurHash64 for fingerprinting; consider migrating to hardware-accelerated CRC if CPU becomes a bottleneck
We intentionally keep reservoir TTL short (default 45s) to match observed conversational burst timescales; make TTL tenant-configurable
If kernel-signature confidence is low, scheduler falls back to cold kernel selection path to avoid mis-specialization
Future: consider per-tenant reservoir weighting to prioritize high-SLA customers during tight memory pressure
